The mechanism is the same goal process cut by time: first-half goal rate is below the full-match average share, early dynamics are cautious, and half-specific dependence leads to many 0-0 and 1-1 first halves. Lineup information and game-state dynamics matter differently by half, and added time at half-time interacts with rules text.

interactions.hypothesis: Propagating strength uncertainty into the simulation flattens title/relegation probabilities relative to fixed-strength sims; the flattening is largest for the favourites and near the cut.
Schedule matters most when the table is tight and tiebreaks (H2H, GD) decide; the interaction is non-linear near cut-off.
Teams in multiple competitions with thin squads lose more strength in the league run-in, so depth interacts with cup progression.
A deduction changes who reaches a tiebreak and which tiebreak applies, creating non-additive effects in relegation and qualification markets.

season_outcome.mechanism: Season-outcome futures (title, top-N, relegation, qualification, advancement, outright, host, trophies) are the outcome of a stochastic tournament: remaining fixtures are simulated from team strengths with uncertainty and drift, then tiebreak and slot rules are applied. The mechanism is the aggregate of many match outcomes, so value comes from correct rating uncertainty, schedule strength, rule details, squad depth and injuries, and correlation across teams. Long-horizon prices embed more information drift than match prices, so the underlying rating prior and rule parsing matter most.
season_outcome.target: Final league position/qualification/advancement or trophy outcome, as defined by competition rules and the contract wording.

season_stat.mechanism: Season-stat markets (team points, points margin, player total, season leader) settle on an accumulated count over remaining fixtures. The mechanism is a sum of match-level processes (points or goals) with strength uncertainty, rotation and injury risk, and tie-break or rounding rules. m.ladder_structure.label: Cross-rung consistency of the threshold ladder
m.ladder_structure.measurement: Collect all rungs of an event at one timestamp; check monotonicity of cumulative prices; fit a constrained distribution (bivariate Poisson / negative binomial for goals) by least squares on mid prices and record per-rung residuals and implied pmf.
m.ladder_structure.mechanism: Adjacent threshold markets (over 1.5/2.5/3.5 goals, handicap steps) must form a monotone cumulative distribution; violations or kinks expose mispriced rungs and the implied distribution of the underlying count.
m.ladder_structure.rationale: Each rung is priced separately by different participants, so the implied pmf (differences between adjacent cumulative prices) can go negative or be implausibly lumpy. Fitting a smooth parametric distribution across rungs and trading the residual is a market-structure edge that does not depend on a view about the teams. Subtle: push rules and integer vs half-point lines change which rung differences are legitimate.

soc.travel_timezone.mechanism: Long trips and time-zone shifts impair recovery and sleep, relevant in continental cups, national-team tournaments and clubs with remote away fixtures.
soc.travel_timezone.rationale: The effect is small domestically but meaningful for intercontinental fixtures and for teams returning from international duty across time zones; hard to isolate from rest and opponent. Subtle: direction of travel (eastward worse) and kickoff local time matter; sample sizes are limited.

soc.var_intervention_rate.label: VAR intervention and penalty/disallowed-goal rates
soc.var_intervention_rate.measurement: Per league: reviews, overturns, penalties and disallowed goals per match; per referee/VAR pair random effects with shrinkage; interact with penalty-rate input.
soc.var_intervention_rate.mechanism: VAR reviews add disallowed goals and penalties and lengthen stoppage time, altering goal totals slightly and settlement timing.
soc.var_intervention_rate.rationale: VAR-era baselines differ by league and by referee/VAR pairs; the VAR official is often announced with the referee. Subtle: effects are small and noisy; they matter most for exact-score and first-scorer markets where disallowed goals shift outcomes.

soc.weather.label: Weather/pitch/altitude
soc.weather.measurement: Pull hourly forecast at kickoff +0..2h at venue lat/lon: wind speed/gust, precipitation, temperature, humidity; regress total goals and shot quality on these with league fixed effects; interact with roofed/artificial flags.
soc.weather.mechanism: Heavy rain, strong wind, extreme heat and altitude change ball control, passing accuracy and stamina, shifting goal expectation and variance.
soc.weather.rationale: Wind and rain reduce passing/shooting quality and tend to lower totals and favour direct teams; extreme heat reduces pressing. Forecasts are knowable pregame (updated through the morning), but the effect is modest and measured across many matches. Subtle: stadium roofs and pitch type (artificial/hybrid) neutralise or alter effects; use kickoff-hour forecast at the stadium coordinates rather than city averages.

soc.xg.label: Team xG for/against, shot quality, set-piece xG
soc.xg.measurement: Per team-match: open-play xG for/against excluding penalties and own goals, set-piece xG separately; exponentially time-weight (half-life ~ 8-12 league matches, tuned by CV), adjust for opponent and venue via a ridge/hierarchical regression (see soc.xg_adjusted_ratings), shrink to league mean by n/(n+k) with k ~ 8-10 matches.
soc.xg.mechanism: Shot-quality-weighted chance creation and prevention is a lower-noise estimate of underlying goal-scoring ability than realised goals, which carry large finishing and keeper variance.
soc.xg.rationale: Goals are rare and noisy; xG counts what a typical finisher would score from the same shot locations, so the sum over a sample converges to future goal rate faster than goals do. Subtle: xG models differ by provider, xG should be split open play / set piece / penalty, and raw averages are biased by schedule and game state. Using it unadjusted for opponent and venue rewards teams that padded stats against weak opposition.

soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.label: Opponent- and venue-adjusted xG attack/defence ratings
soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.measurement: For each match, log(xG_for) ~ attack_i + defence_j + home + league intercept with ridge penalty (or Bayesian hierarchical with team random effects) fitted by rolling windows with exponential decay; evaluate by out-of-sample log-loss vs raw xG ratings.
soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.mechanism: A joint regression of per-match xG on team attack, opposition defence and home effects strips schedule effects so each team's rating reflects its quality, not its fixtures.
soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.rationale: Raw xG averages mix quality with opposition strength and with game state. A ridge/hierarchical model identifies attack and defence parameters with shrinkage that handles sparse samples and rotates through league structure. Subtle: cross-league comparisons need linking data, and using season-end ratings in a backtest leaks future results.

soc.xi_strength_delta.label: Confirmed XI quality vs season-average XI
soc.xi_strength_delta.measurement: Player value per position from regression of team xG-diff on minute-weighted player indicators (ridge) or from xG+xA, defensive and GK models; delta = value(XI) minus minutes-weighted mean XI value over the season; split into attack and defence components.
soc.xi_strength_delta.mechanism: Team quality in a given match equals the sum of the quality of the 11 actually fielded; the deviation from the typical XI is the expected-goal shift from rotation and absence.
soc.xi_strength_delta.rationale: This turns lineup news into a number comparable across teams, and interacts with xG ratings (fatigued first choice vs rested reserve). It is available only after lineup release; before that, a probabilistic estimate (soc.rotation_index) is needed. Subtle: position-specific replacement matters more than the sum, and attacking and defensive contributions must be tracked separately.
